cards.title: Use product-quiz answers for recommendations and customer research
cards.summary: When building a store quiz that must select products and reveal buyer preferences.
cards.use_when: When building a store quiz that must select products and reveal buyer preferences.
steps: Define which SKU, size, format or bundle each question can change before adding the question.
Ask about intended use, current routine, preferences, compatibility and previous product frustrations. Skip demographic or health questions that do not affect a valid product choice.
Map answers to real recommendation rules and export answer distributions by traffic source.
Compare frequent needs with the assumed avatar; use the language in new ad hooks and identify gaps in the assortment.
caveats: Respondents represent the traffic sent to the quiz, not the entire market.
Merchant application of the source framework; not a source-demonstrated ecommerce result.

cards.title: Place useful explanation screens between product-quiz questions
cards.summary: When shoppers abandon a quiz or cannot understand why a preference matters.
cards.use_when: When shoppers abandon a quiz or cannot understand why a preference matters.
steps: Test an explanation after roughly three to five questions, the source heuristic.
Branch the explanation on actual answers: explain why a selected use case needs a particular material, fit or format.
Use genuine customer evidence only; a percentage comparison needs an actual measured population.
Measure step abandonment and downstream purchases, not completion alone.
caveats: Three to five questions is a source heuristic, not an optimum.
Merchant application of the source framework; not a source-demonstrated ecommerce result.

cards.title: Choose quiz input controls that fit product decisions
cards.summary: When a product quiz repeats many identical button screens.
cards.use_when: When a product quiz repeats many identical button screens.
steps: Use single choice for mutually exclusive formats, multi-select for preferences, and numeric input for a relevant size or consumption amount.
Avoid adding questions merely to lengthen the quiz. Each field must improve selection or useful research.
Keep keyboard and mobile interaction usable; map every control to a stable exported field.
Test a preference slider only if it is easier than buttons for this choice.
caveats: The source had not tested its proposed slider interaction.
Merchant application of the source framework; not a source-demonstrated ecommerce result.

cards.title: Reflect product preferences in later quiz copy
cards.summary: When a recommendation quiz feels generic despite collecting useful answers.
cards.use_when: When a recommendation quiz feels generic despite collecting useful answers.
steps: Branch later copy on selected use, format and prior frustrations.
Show how a recommended product solves the named practical constraint; never claim every shopper needs the same SKU while implying individualized matching.
Limit branches to combinations the team can test and maintain.
Test incompatible and contradictory answer combinations before launch.
caveats: Merchant application of the source framework; not a source-demonstrated ecommerce result.

cards.title: Reveal the product-match explanation before the buy box
cards.summary: When shoppers need to understand why a quiz recommends a particular SKU or bundle.
cards.use_when: When shoppers need to understand why a quiz recommends a particular SKU or bundle.
steps: Summarize the actual answers that determine the recommendation.
Show the matching SKU, size or bundle and explain the rule connecting it to those answers.
If calculating replenishment, show the consumption assumption and let the shopper correct it.
Follow with product details, price, relevant genuine reviews, delivery and returns, then a purchase CTA.
caveats: Do not simulate computation or invent medical outcomes, future-body projections or guaranteed result dates.
Merchant application of the source framework; not a source-demonstrated ecommerce result.

cards.title: Use an occasion date to check product delivery suitability
cards.summary: When recommending products for gifts, travel, events or a move.
cards.use_when: When recommending products for gifts, travel, events or a move.
steps: Ask the occasion and needed-by date only if timing changes the recommendation.
Compare that date with actual stock, handling and delivery estimates.
Show suitable products and explain any delivery uncertainty before checkout.
Use genuine order deadlines where applicable; do not add resetting scarcity timers.
caveats: Merchant application of the source framework; not a source-demonstrated ecommerce result.

cards.title: Use routine and consumption to recommend a starter configuration
cards.summary: When a store must choose a product format, starter kit or replenishment interval.
cards.use_when: When a store must choose a product format, starter kit or replenishment interval.
steps: Ask what the shopper already uses, how often, what failed previously and what routine is realistic.
Map those answers to a starter configuration or replenishment interval.
Respect exclusions and explicit dislikes in both the main recommendation and cross-sells.
Let the shopper adjust the suggested quantity or subscription before purchase.
caveats: Merchant application of the source framework; not a source-demonstrated ecommerce result.

cards.title: Keep the quiz result page focused on a transparent product offer
cards.summary: When quiz completion is strong but product purchases are weak.
cards.use_when: When quiz completion is strong but product purchases are weak.
steps: Make the answer summary, recommended product and offered price consistent.
Remove unrelated outbound distractions while preserving access to delivery, returns, product details and support.
If offering to email results, explain what will be sent and capture marketing preferences separately.
Compare the full quiz-to-purchase journey with direct-to-PDP traffic; test one major change at a time.
caveats: The source uses a subscription-app example. Long quizzes and commitment steps are hypotheses, not guaranteed retail improvements.
Merchant application of the source framework; not a source-demonstrated ecommerce result.
